newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to resume discussion on forex decontrol.
newsitem.headline: Japan to resume discussion on forex decontrol.

text.p: A key Japanese government panel will start discussion on deregulation of foreign exchange operations so that it can submit a bill for revision of the foreign exchange law to the next ordinary parliament session, financial sources said on Wednesday.

The Committee on Foreign Exchange and Other Transactions, an advisory panel to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), will start discussing on Thursday ways to allow corporations to engage in foreign exchange business currently limited to banks.
The Committee will discuss in detail the qualifications of new participants, a range of foreign exchange business they can cover, and the role of supervisors.
In June, the committee called for revisions and a comprehensive overhaul of the Tokyo forex market but details and the timing of deregulation were not decided.

Financial sources said the areas of business that new participants are allowed to do would include currency exchanges and loans to overseas companies and derivatives. Regular banking business such as foreign currency deposits and overseas remittance would be excluded, the sources said.
A MOF source said details have not been decided but added that too much supervision would undermine efforts to stimulate the Tokyo foreign exchange market.
